# QR setup dependencies

QR setup transports the existing private pairing invitation. Generation and
scanning happen locally; no cloud API, model download or Google Play services is
used. Only Android's explicit scan action requests camera permission.

| Component | Pinned source / package | License and packaging |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows encoder | [skip2/go-qrcode](https://github.com/skip2/go-qrcode/tree/da1b6568686e89143e94f980a98bc2dbd5537f13), `v0.0.0-20200617195104-da1b6568686e` in `go.mod` / `go.sum` | MIT; `QR-CODE-NOTICE.txt` copied beside the Windows executable |
| Android camera UI and decoder integration | [ZXing Android Embedded 4.3.0](https://github.com/journeyapps/zxing-android-embedded/tree/v4.3.0), Maven Central `com.journeyapps:zxing-android-embedded:4.3.0` | Apache-2.0; bundled in APK, notice/license available in Open-source notices |
| Android QR decoding | [ZXing core 3.5.4](https://github.com/zxing/zxing/tree/zxing-3.5.4), Maven Central `com.google.zxing:core:3.5.4` | Apache-2.0; explicitly upgrades the camera library's older transitive core; same notices screen |
| Activity result lifecycle | [AndroidX Activity 1.11.0](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/activity#1.11.0), Google Maven `androidx.activity:activity:1.11.0` | Apache-2.0; same notices screen |
| Media session lifecycle | [AndroidX Media3 Session 1.11.1](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/media3#1.11.1), Google Maven `androidx.media3:media3-session:1.11.1` | Apache-2.0; same notices screen |
| Kotlin runtime | [Kotlin Standard Library 2.2.21](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/tree/v2.2.21), Maven Central `org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib:2.2.21` | Apache-2.0; same notices screen |

These are pinned compatible releases, not a claim that all are the newest.
Gradle resolves their AndroidX support dependencies through the existing official
repositories. APK camera use comes from the bundled library, not an external scan
application. Its activity is explicitly non-exported. Image export and the scan
beep are disabled; only QR format is decoded. Mixed normal/inverted decoding
supports ordinary dark and light terminal themes.

The Go module is pure Go and has no transitive module dependencies. `go mod verify`
checks its downloaded content against `go.sum`. No encoder source is modified.
Low error correction keeps the current invitation, including its quiet zone,
within 80 columns. Two module rows use one Unicode half-block text row. A shared
synthetic terminal fixture is generated by Go and decoded with ZXing in Android
JVM tests to check exact payload preservation and both theme polarities. Manual
camera/terminal checks remain required; unusual fonts or low contrast can impair
scan reliability.

Android licenses/notices are in `qr-assets/qr-notices.txt`; Gradle packages that
asset with the existing WebRTC notices. No camera frames, QR image files or
additional local HTTP endpoints are created by MicDrop.
